ai.purpose: Develop the Inverted Star topology as a structural model for distributed, center-absent relational systems. Demonstrates how meaning and force can radiate from a periphery inward rather than projecting outward from a central node. Establishes the theoretical basis for non-hierarchical structural influence.
ai.summary: Book 2 introduces the Inverted Star as a formal topological construct where structural force flows from peripheral nodes toward an empty or virtual center. This reversal of conventional hub-and-spoke logic enables modeling of emergent, leaderless, and distributed phenomena. The book develops full formal notation and proves key invariants governing inverted-star configurations.

references: INV-IS-001: Center Absence — a valid inverted star has no structurally dominant center node
INV-IS-002: Peripheral Equivalence — all peripheral nodes share equivalent structural weight in the absence of explicit asymmetry declarations
INV-IS-003: Inward Force Propagation — influence vectors point inward; outward propagation constitutes a structural violation
INV-IS-004: Emergence Condition — coherent behavior at the center is a function of peripheral convergence, not central direction
